chunks: What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgot to perform the two rakʿahs of the obligatory tawaf behind the Maqam.
While Allah, the Exalted, has said: “And take from the Maqam of Ibrahim a place of prayer.”
Until he has departed. So he عليه السلام said: If he has departed, then I do not wish to impose hardship upon him, and I do not order him to return; rather, he should pray wherever he remembers.
And it is possible that the earlier reports are to be understood as referring to merit and recommendation, while the later reports indicate permissibility and the lifting of prohibition.

key_terms.ارْتَحَلَ: he departed or moved on from the place
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ: extra merit or virtue beyond bare validity
key_terms.الْمَقَامِ: Maqam Ibrahim, the place behind which the prayer of tawaf is performed
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ: the two units of prayer required here after tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory tawaf for which the prayer is being discussed

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they forget the two rakʿahs of tawaf until after leaving Maqam Ibrahim?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who forgot the two rakʿahs of the obligatory tawaf behind Maqam Ibrahim and only remembered after departing. The Imam عليه السلام states that such a person is not required to return, but should perform the prayer wherever he remembers. The concluding statement reconciles reports by understanding some as expressing recommendation and merit, and others as indicating permissibility.
